derived_from.aggregation: The design point's devices are collapsed into ONE logical device carrying the resource ONE TOKEN can engage: the aggregate divided by that design's own token_slots (4 on the ROM side, 2 on the GPU side).  That is what reproduces each side's published PER-TOKEN component times; carrying the undivided aggregate would remove a different serialisation factor from each side.  Four of the five analytical terms survive the collapse; the fifth, link_latency, is removed by it and is reported as a structural residual, as is the aggregate-throughput view a pipelined design also loses.

description: N5 design-target machine for the ROM role of the analytical anchor pair DSV4-Flash/ROM-N5-native-HBMKV-array-hybrid-x32 vs DSV4-Flash/b200_sxm-x16-hybrid (DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731, batch 1, context 200000).  DERIVED, NOT MEASURED: every parameter here is an analytical value divided by a stated denominator or an explicit statement that the analytical model prices no counterpart, and every entry carries its derivation in `note` and its technology.json grade in `analytical_grade`.  Nothing in this file is characterized; the measured SKY130 and ASAP7 tables are untouched and describe a different machine.  Generated by tools/derive_cycle_machine.py from results/roofline/n5_vs_b200/analytical.json; run that tool with --check to verify this file still matches the anchor it claims.

clock.frequency_hz.note: 3 sequencer cycles (sequencer.fetch_cycles + decode_cycles + issue_cycles, the cycle model's per-instruction front end) divided by technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s.  The analytical model states no clock; this is the one analytical quantity that fixes one.  Every rate below is an analytical B/s or ops/s divided by this clock, so a different clock would move the per-cycle numbers and leave every derived TIME unchanged.

engine.attention.bytes_per_cycle.note: The analytical model prices no engine byte-port bandwidth.  Both machines are given the larger of the pair's weight-path rates (1.210496e+15 B/s) so that no simulated time is attributed to an engine port the analytical model does not model.  At the shipped 64 B/cycle this would throttle DMA to 6.400e+10 B/s, 18914x below the ROM array it drains.

engine.attention.fixed_latency_cycles.note: technology.json#latency.pipeline_fill_drain_s 3.2e-08 s + one global wire traversal sqrt(reticle.area_mm2) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm = 4.282231e-09 s, the analytical array-pass boundary 3.628223e-08 s, times the clock = 36.2822 cycles.  The analytical model charges 4 of these per layer; the cycle model charges one per engine instruction and has no per-layer hook, so the difference between the deployment's instructions per layer and 4 is a reported residual, not a tuned parameter.

engine.attention.lanes.default.note: Same as engine.tensor.lanes.default.  The analytical model prices all arithmetic at one roof and names no engine families, so every family is given the same width and the same per-lane depth.  For 'attention' the cycle model divides tile work by lanes x work_per_lane_cycle directly, so the product is the whole story.

engine.attention.queue_depth.default.note: Carried unchanged from configs/hardware/abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json, where it is graded assumed and is a node-independent descriptor count.  The analytical model prices no queue occupancy.

engine.tensor.lanes.default.note: The narrowest tensor operator output width in DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 (64: index_head_weights), read from build/ir-v3/deepseek-v4-flash-0731/kernel_ir.v3.json over the 879 kernels it declares with counter_class tensor.  At batch 1 the cycle model's tensor rate is min(lanes, tile_cols*issue_window, cols) x work_per_lane_cycle x clock, so lanes above the operator's own output width are masked and deliver nothing.  64 is the largest lane count for which EVERY tensor operator of this model runs at the full derived roof; at 256 the MAC-weighted achieved rate falls to 99.8% of the roof; at 512 the MAC-weighted achieved rate falls to 99.2% of the roof.  The pair (lanes, work_per_lane_cycle) is a gauge split of one analytical quantity -- their product times the clock is what the design point pins -- and this rule fixes the split by exactness.

engine.tensor.work_per_lane_cycle.note: compute roof / (lanes x clock), in work-counter units.  The roof is the design point's OWN arithmetic over the design point's OWN published time: fp32 67764224 + w4a8 49897275392 = 49965039616 operations / component_times_s.compute 0.00010046345634363994 s = 4.9734541727e+14 ops/s.  That identity is exact by construction, which is the point: a literal 'bf16' index into operations_by_canonical_format raises on a w4a8 design point and a literal 'bf16' compute density prices one 2.7x too slow WITHOUT raising.  Cross-checked against the technology derivation the study built the term from -- sum over formats of ops_f / (area_fractions.compute 0.07644864468546485 x silicon_area_mm2 26080.0 x compute_ops_s_per_mm2[f] x efficiencies.compute 0.55), times token_slots 4 -- which gives 1.004634563436399e-04 s against the published 1.004634563436399e-04 s, agreeing to +0.000e+00 relative.  Units: the cost table declares this parameter in work/lane/cycle and the shipped characterized value was measured as (tensor.multiplications + tensor.additions) / cycles; the analytical operations count is a work count too, at 3.84346 operations per active parameter (real operator accounting, NOT the multiply-and-add fallback), so no conversion is needed and none is applied.  That makes the machine's MAC rate lanes x work_per_lane_cycle / 3.84346 x clock = 1.2940028617e+14 MAC/s.  In the cycle model this value divides the K extent (ceil(tile_depth x work_scale / work_per_lane_cycle)), so it is the reduction-tree width of one output lane -- 2021.88 MACs deep -- and not a second lane count.

hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel.note: One HBM3E channel, taken from the GPU point and shared: points[GPU].kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read x token_slots 2 = 1.152000e+14 B/s of physical pool over 16 packages x 8 stacks x 8 channels = 1.125000e+11 B/s per channel = 112.5 B/cycle at this clock.  The COUNT each collapsed logical device carries is that design's provisioning divided by the slots a token traverses: the GPU role gets 512 channels for 5.760000e+13 B/s and the ROM role 320 channels for 3.600000e+13 B/s of KV.  The two design points buy different numbers of the SAME channel, which is why hbm.channels is the only HBM parameter the two machines are permitted to differ on.

hbm.channels.default.note: 40 HBM3E stacks x 8 channels.  points[ROM].area_fractions.hbm_phy 0.06134969325153374 of 815 mm2 per device at 10 mm2 per stack over 32 devices, divided by token_slots 4 because a token engages one slot at a time, serving KV alone at 3.600000e+13 B/s (kv_transfer_bytes_per_step / component_times_s.kv_read).

hbm.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to the HBM burst so consecutive bursts stripe across channels.

hbm.read_latency_cycles.note: The analytical layer_fixed_latency charges one KV round trip per layer: sram_access_s 2e-09 + one global traversal 4.282231e-09 = 6.282231e-09 s = 6.2822 cycles.  points[GPU] holds KV in 'hbm' and points[ROM] in 'hbm'; the primitive is a round trip to whichever store holds it, so it is charged identically on both machines and is shared.

hbm.transaction_bytes.note: 225 B = 2 x hbm.bytes_per_cycle_per_channel, the smallest integer burst for which the cycle model's ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle) is exact and no channel bandwidth is lost to quantisation.  The analytical model has no burst-size concept.

hbm.write_latency_cycles.note: The analytical layer_fixed_latency charges one KV round trip per layer: sram_access_s 2e-09 + one global traversal 4.282231e-09 = 6.282231e-09 s = 6.2822 cycles.  points[GPU] holds KV in 'hbm' and points[ROM] in 'hbm'; the primitive is a round trip to whichever store holds it, so it is charged identically on both machines and is shared.

host.bytes_per_cycle.note: Host management path, carried unchanged from abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json.  The analytical model has no host term and no decode-step traffic crosses this path.

host.latency_cycles.note: Host management path, carried unchanged from abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json.  The analytical model has no host term and no decode-step traffic crosses this path.

host.transaction_bytes.note: Host management path, carried unchanged from abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json.  The analytical model has no host term and no decode-step traffic crosses this path.

model.max_modeled_transactions_per_acces.note: A simulator fidelity knob, not a machine parameter; carried unchanged.  Above it an access reserves per-unit time in bulk, which keeps total occupancy exact and only coarsens the interleave.

queue.transit_cycles.note: Not priced by the analytical model.  Carried unchanged from configs/hardware/abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json, where it is graded assumed and is a node-independent cycle count; the run's issue_cycles, queue_stall_cycles and wait_stall_cycles counters report its contribution separately, so it is attributed rather than zeroed.

rom.arrays.default.note: 64 independently-addressable ROM arrays, the ROM bank count declared by the base capability this pair is emitted against (memory.rom.banks; the ROM lowering stripes one bank per weight role).  The analytical model fixes only the product arrays x bytes_per_cycle_per_array x clock, so this is the granularity choice and the next parameter is the consequence.  NOTE: the shipped ROM capabilities advertise this under the key 'banks', which MachineModel.structural does not read (it looks for memory.rom.arrays), so the shipped ROM runs silently used the cost table's default of 8.  The emitted capability advertises both keys.

rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array.note: The ROM weight rate ONE TOKEN engages: the design point's aggregate array rate peak_weight_read_bytes_s 4.8419165508e+15 B/s (= rom area 17791.8193 mm2 x technology_derivations.rom_read_bytes_s_per_mm2 x efficiencies.rom_read_bandwidth, already derated) divided by token_slots 4, because a token traverses 4 slot(s) in series and can engage only one of them at a time = 1.2104791377e+15 B/s.  That reproduces the published per-token term: points[ROM].stored_weight_bytes 166878536440 / that rate = 1.378616e-04 s against component_times_s.weight_read 0.00013786155518438986 s.  Divided by 64 arrays and by the clock = 18913.736526, rounded to 18914.  Achieved aggregate 1.2104960000e+15 B/s, +0.00139% against the analytical value.

rom.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to the ROM burst so consecutive bursts of one weight object land on consecutive arrays and a sweep engages every array.

rom.read_latency_cycles.note: The analytical model prices no ROM access latency.  The ROM array is on die, so the one analytical latency primitive that applies is a global wire traversal of the reticle: sqrt(reticle.area_mm2 815.0) x global_wire_delay_s_per_mm 1.5e-10 = 4.282231e-09 s = 4.2822 cycles.

rom.transaction_bytes.note: Set equal to rom.bytes_per_cycle_per_array so that the cycle model's max(1, ceil(transaction_bytes / bytes_per_cycle)) is exactly 1 and the array delivers its full derived rate.  The analytical model has no burst-size concept, so this is the only constraint on the value.

sequencer.branch_cycles.note: Not priced by the analytical model.  Carried unchanged from configs/hardware/abi3_cost_sky130_rom_v2.json, where it is graded assumed and is a node-independent cycle count; the run's issue_cycles, queue_stall_cycles and wait_stall_cycles counters report its contribution separately, so it is attributed rather than zeroed.

sequencer.decode_cycles.note: The cycle model's instruction decode.  These three are the machine's per-instruction front end and their sum is what technology.json#latency.sequencer_issue_decode_s = 3e-09 s prices; that identity is what fixes clock.frequency_hz, so they cannot be changed without changing the clock.

sram.banks.default.note: 32 banks, the bank count the shipped single-chip capabilities on both sides already declare, kept so the compiled bank masks mean what they meant before.  points[ROM] allocates area_fractions.sram 0.0 and points[GPU] 0.0; the analytical model prices no bank count on either side, so this is a granularity choice shared by construction.

sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.note: The GPU design point prices NO SRAM term and allocates no SRAM area (area_fractions.sram 0.0), so there is nothing to reproduce.  banks x ports x this rate x clock = 2.097152e+15 B/s, which exceeds every rate this pair derives (1.210479e+15 B/s) so that the activation store cannot bind and no simulated time is attributed to a store the analytical model does not price.  This is a deliberate neutralisation for a validation experiment: the derived machine is NOT a complete machine and its absolute tokens/s is an upper bound.

sram.interleave_bytes.note: Set equal to the SRAM burst so consecutive bursts stripe across ports.  See sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.

sram.ports_per_bank.default.note: Chosen with sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port.  See that parameter.

sram.transaction_bytes.note: Set equal to sram.bytes_per_cycle_per_port so the model's ceil() is exact.  See that parameter.

state.backing_storage_class.note: STATE objects are timed as if they lived in SRAM, unchanged from the shipped tables.  ADR-003 does not bind the placement of a state resource and the analytical model has no state term.
